causes.text: Spirit AeroSystems, a key fuselage supplier, disclosed that on certain single-aisle fuselages the fittings joining the aft fuselage to the vertical tail were installed using a non-standard process, implying inspections and targeted rework.

source_info.title: Boeing halts deliveries of some 737 MAXs amid new supplier problem

effects.text: The airframer paused a subset of single-aisle deliveries to identify and rework affected units; shares closed down about 5.6% on 2023-04-14 as investors priced in schedule disruption and remediation costs.

source_info.title: Boeing shares tumble as some MAX deliveries halted over parts issue

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Supplier non-conformance on load-bearing aft-fuselage fittings raises immediate quality risk.
Final assembler pauses a portion of deliveries to scope, inspect, and rework affected airframes.
Equity market discounts added cost and timing risk; BA ends the day down 5.6%.

rationale: A supplier quality lapse triggered a targeted delivery pause and a same-day stock selloff documented by major outlets.
counterfactual_analysis: If the fittings had been installed per specification, no pause would have been required and the 5.6% decline was unlikely.

adversarial_confounders.impact: Could have influenced the magnitude of the decline.

details.commentary: Boeing's reliance on a small number of complex, safety-critical fuselage suppliers gives those partners outsized influence over its production rhythm. When Spirit AeroSystems discloses a process deviation that requires inspections and rework, this concentrated supplier structure magnifies the disruption to Boeing's deliveries and costs.
